views.name: classroom_capacity_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  CASE
    WHEN classroom.capacity IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
    WHEN classroom.capacity < 25 THEN '0-24'
    WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 25 AND 49 THEN '25-49'
    WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 50 AND 99 THEN '50-99'
    WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 100 AND 199 THEN '100-199'
    ELSE '200+'
  END AS capacity_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS classroom_count,
  -- include PKs to keep view joinable
  MIN(classroom.room_number) AS sample_room_number
FROM classroom
GROUP BY classroom.building,
  CASE
    WHEN classroom.capacity IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
    WHEN classroom.capacity < 25 THEN '0-24'
    WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 25 AND 49 THEN '25-49'
    WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 50 AND 99 THEN '50-99'
    WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 100 AND 199 THEN '100-199'
    ELSE '200+'
  END

params.description: Counts of classrooms per building broken into capacity buckets (e.g., 0-24, 25-49, etc.).
params.when_to_use: When you need distribution of classroom counts by building and capacity ranges | To build dashboards or reports that show how many rooms of each size exist per building | As a pre-aggregated input when joining classroom capacity distributions to other building-level data (e.g., facilities, maintenance, building footprint) | To compose further SQL that aggregates across buildings or capacity_bucket (for totals, percentages, shares)
params.output_schema: building: building identifier from classroom.building (source column classroom.building) | capacity_bucket: categorical bucket computed from classroom.capacity with values 'unknown', '0-24', '25-49', '50-99', '100-199', '200+' (derived from classroom.capacity via CASE expression shown in view SQL) | classroom_count: count of classroom rows in that building and capacity_bucket (derived as COUNT(*) over grouped rows) | sample_room_number: an example room_number from the grouped rows (derived as MIN(classroom.room_number) included to keep view joinable; not part of the primary metric)
params.metric: classroom_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of classroom rows per (building, capacity_bucket) | capacity_bucket = CASE WHEN classroom.capacity IS NULL THEN 'unknown' WHEN classroom.capacity < 25 THEN '0-24' WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 25 AND 49 THEN '25-49' WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 50 AND 99 THEN '50-99' WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 100 AND 199 THEN '100-199' ELSE '200+' END | sample_room_number = MIN(classroom.room_number)  -- non-aggregated helper sample value; not a measure for summation
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a building-level dimension (for example a view or table keyed by building) ON classroom_capacity_by_building.building = building_dim.building — safe because this view is one row per (building, capacity_bucket) and joining to a one-row-per-building dimension will not duplicate classroom_count. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: you may aggregate this view first (e.g., SUM(classroom_count) GROUP BY building) and then join to other building-level datasets without risk of duplication because the aggregation collapses the capacity_bucket axis. | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many table or view keyed to building that has multiple rows per building (for example a table of building rooms, maintenance events, or any joinable view that is one-to-many with building) without re-aggregating either side — such joins will multiply classroom_count because classroom_capacity_by_building already contains counts at the (building, capacity_bucket) grain. | do NOT join to section-level or course-level views (e.g., section_with_course_instructor_room_time) on building or room fields unless you first aggregate those details to the same (building, capacity_bucket) grain or aggregate this view to the join key; section-level joins are many-to-one relative to classroom counts and will duplicate measures. | When composing further: if you need rates or shares (e.g., proportion of rooms in a bucket per building), compute them by aggregating classroom_count into the desired denominator in SQL (for example, SUM(classroom_count) OVER (PARTITION BY building) to get total rooms per building) rather than joining to another many-row dataset to obtain denominators. | Safe pattern examples: (a) to get total rooms per building: SELECT building, SUM(classroom_count) AS total_rooms FROM classroom_capacity_by_building GROUP BY building; (b) to attach building attributes: SELECT b.*, c.classroom_count, c.capacity_bucket FROM classroom_capacity_by_building c JOIN building_dim b ON c.building = b.building; | Unsafe pattern examples: joining classroom_capacity_by_building to takes_with_student_course_section (section rows per room/time) directly on building or room will duplicate classroom_count because sections are many-per-room; instead first aggregate sections to building (or to building+capacity_bucket if possible) then join.

otherwise deduplicate the department side before joining to avoid duplicating instructor rows. | safe composition example: SELECT b.ID, b.name, b.dept_name, agg.sections_count FROM instructor_basic b JOIN (SELECT instructor_ID AS ID, COUNT(*) AS sections_count FROM section_with_course_instructor_room_time GROUP BY instructor_ID) agg USING (ID); params.when_to_use: Fetch student attributes together with the advisor i_ID for use in joins or filtering (e.g., find a student's advisor id, list students with advisor pointers). | Compose queries that need per-student measures (tot_cred) plus advisor linkage without aggregating across students. | Build higher-level joins that enrich each student row (e.g., join to department info, enrollment summaries, or latest advisor) while preserving a one-row-per-student grain.
params.output_schema: ID: the student's unique identifier; sourced from student.ID | student_name: the student's name; sourced from student.name | dept_name: the department name that the student belongs to; sourced from student.dept_name | tot_cred: the student's total credits (per-student scalar); sourced from student.tot_cred | advisor_i_ID: the identifier (i_ID) on the advisor row that references this student; sourced from advisor.i_ID

otherwise measures on students_with_advisors_33 will be duplicated. | If you need counts or sums of related rows per student, perform the aggregation on the related table first (produce one row per student), then join that result to this view on ID — this preserves correct per-student measures. | Because the view is defined by student JOIN advisor ON advisor.s_ID = student.ID, it returns only students that have at least one advisor row; if advisor can be many-to-one (multiple advisor rows per student) then this view's grain is effectively one-row-per-(student,advisor) and is NOT safe to treat as strictly one-row-per-student unless you know advisor.s_ID is unique. If advisor.s_ID is unique (one advisor row per student), then the view is one-row-per-student and joins as described above are safe.

params.description: Rows of instructors teaching specific course sections in a particular semester and year (one row per instructor-course-section-term).
params.when_to_use: List instructors assigned to teach a given course section in a given semester and year | Filter or join teaching assignments by course, section, instructor ID, semester or year | Compose with section, course, classroom, or enrollment data to produce richer section-level reports | Use as the driving set when you need one row per teaching assignment by term (safe base for further aggregation)

params.metric: No derived aggregate metrics in this view; all outputs are base columns projected directly from teaches. | If you need counts or other aggregates (e.g., number of instructors per section), compute them by aggregating this view (e.g., COUNT(*) GROUP BY course_id, sec_id, semester, year).

Instead, aggregate the student-side data to the (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) level (for example, COUNT(student_id) GROUP BY course_id, sec_id, semester, year) and then join back to this view. | Do NOT join directly to course_prereq_edges (recursion/edge list) expecting a one-to-one match — prereq edges are many-to-many across courses and will duplicate rows unless you pre-aggregate or otherwise constrain the join keys. | When composing aggregates that count or sum over students or enrollments, perform aggregation on the child (many) side to the view's grain (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) and then join, so measures remain correct and are not inflated. | If you need to produce counts of instructors per section-term, aggregate this view by (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) to create a one-row-per-section-term result, then join other dimension tables at that section-term grain.

views.name: course_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course

params.description: A canonical per-course row giving each course's identifier, department name, and credit value.
params.when_to_use: Look up basic course attributes (department and credits) for a specific course_id or set of course_ids. | Join course-level attributes onto other datasets keyed by course_id (e.g., sections, enrollments, prerequisites) without causing duplication when done correctly. | Compose higher-level aggregates that need course-level denominators or attributes (e.g., average credits per department) using this view as the course-level grain.
params.output_schema: course_id: the unique identifier of the course — derived from course.course_id in the base table. | dept_name: the department name that offers the course — derived from course.dept_name in the base table. | credits: the credit value assigned to the course — derived from course.credits in the base table.
params.metric: course_id = course.course_id  -- identity column, primary key at the view grain (one row per course_id) | dept_name = course.dept_name  -- descriptive attribute, not an aggregate | credits = course.credits      -- numeric attribute at course grain (treat as a measure when aggregating, but it is stored per-course here)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to section_with_course_instructor_room_time ON course_id — safe when joining this view (one-row-per-course) to a section-level view because the planner must expect that section_with_course_instructor_room_time is one-to-many (multiple sections per course). If you intend to keep course-level measures (e.g., credits) aggregated at the course grain, do NOT simply join and sum without accounting for multiplicity; instead, either aggregate sections or use DISTINCT course_id before aggregating to avoid duplicating credits. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to takes_with_student_course_section ON course_id — NOT safe to preserve course-level measures if you then aggregate over students/rows without re-aggregation. takes_with_student_course_section is many-per-course (many student enrollments), so joining will replicate the course row for each enrollment. To use credits as a course-level attribute in student-level analysis, reference credits directly or compute averages using GROUP BY student after appropriate handling (e.g., AVG(credits) OVER (PARTITION ...)) or pre-aggregate courses. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course_prereq_edges ON course_id OR prereq_course_id — safe for attributing course fields to the edge rows (the join will be many-to-one from edges to course), but be aware that joining on course_id or prereq_course_id will expand rows according to the edges relation. If you want counts per course, aggregate after the join; do not expect credits to remain a single-row measure after joining without re-aggregation. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course_offering_counts_by_term ON course_id — safe to enrich offering-count aggregates with course attributes because course_offering_counts_by_term is an aggregate keyed by course_id (one row per course_id per term). The join does not duplicate course-level attributes as long as course_offering_counts_by_term remains at its aggregated grain. If you denormalize to a finer grain (e.g., section), re-aggregate course measures appropriately. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course_popularity_by_enrollment ON course_id — safe because that view is an aggregate per-course (popularity metrics computed per course_id). Joining will attach course attributes without duplicating course-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom_rows or classroom_location_normalized — NOT directly relevant (no shared key); only join if you first join through a section or other join that relates courses to classrooms. Be cautious: joining via section will introduce a one-to-many expansion (sections per course), so re-aggregate as needed. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor_salary_by_department ON dept_name — safe because instructor_salary_by_department is keyed by department (aggregates per department). This is a many-courses-to-one-department join that does not duplicate department-level aggregates if you treat department aggregates as attributes; if you subsequently aggregate by course you must be mindful that department-level metrics will be repeated per course row — to prevent double-counting, aggregate department metrics at the department grain or use window/partitioned expressions. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to student_enrollment_counts ON course_id — only safe if student_enrollment_counts is aggregated per course_id; attaching course attributes to those aggregates is fine. If student_enrollment_counts is at a finer grain (e.g., per student-course), re-aggregation is required to avoid duplicating course attributes. | general rule: this view is strictly one-row-per course_id (course-level grain). It is safe to join to other datasets that are at the same or coarser grain keyed by course_id or dept_name (e.g., per-course aggregates, per-department aggregates). Do NOT join this view to one-to-many detail tables (e.g., enrollments, sections, timeslots) and then treat the result as if still at course grain without re-aggregating, because that will multiply course rows and therefore duplicate course attributes/measures. When composing, either (a) join to aggregates keyed by course_id, (b) aggregate the joined result back to course_id, or (c) use DISTINCT course_id before joining to preserve course-level cardinality.

If you need totals from those child tables, aggregate the child table to one-row-per-course (e.g., COUNT(section_id) GROUP BY course_id) and then join to this view on course_id. | Do NOT join to recursive or edge views (example: course_prereq_edges) without care: joining raw edges will produce multiple rows per course for each prereq relation and thus duplicate course-level columns; instead aggregate prereq counts or materialize prereq sets per course before joining. | When composing with sibling aggregated views (for example: course_popularity_by_enrollment, student_enrollment_counts, course_offering_counts_by_term), ensure those aggregates are computed grouped by course_id (or otherwise reduced to one row per course) before joining on course_id to avoid duplication. | If you need to compute department-level metrics (for example total budget per building or average credits per department), perform those computations from department or aggregate this view grouped by dept_name — do not join this view to raw many-side tables first. | Summary guidance for planners: treat this view as one-row-per-course (grain = course_id) with no internal aggregations. Safe joins are those where the other side is one-row-per-course or one-row-per-department keyed by course_id or dept_name respectively; any join to a one-to-many side must be preceded by aggregation or de-duplication on that side.

They are safe provided you join on keys that are one-to-one or many-to-one from the other side (course_cleaned -> dimension). | composition pattern recommendation: when composing measures, prefer these patterns to preserve correctness: (A) join course_cleaned to a pre-aggregated per-course metric view (e.g., course_popularity_by_enrollment, course_offering_counts_by_term aggregated to course-level) — no re-aggregation needed; (B) join to raw many-side tables (sections, takes) only when you will immediately re-aggregate by course_id to produce correct per-course metrics (use GROUP BY course_id); (C) avoid joining multiple many-side tables simultaneously without performing separate aggregations first, because cross-multiplication can occur.

views.description: Canonical, cleaned catalog of courses (one row per course) with non-null title, credits, and department name.

views.name: course_prereq_links
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prereq.course_id AS course_id,
  prereq.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM prereq

params.description: Lists direct prerequisite links between courses (one row per course -> prerequisite course pair).
params.when_to_use: To find which courses are direct prerequisites of a given course (or which courses a given course is a prerequisite for). | As a base relation when building a graph of course prerequisites (edges) for path/graph queries. | When joining course-level attributes (title, department, etc.) onto prerequisite edges to analyze relationships between course pairs. | When counting or aggregating prerequisites per course (after appropriate grouping/aggregation).
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier for the course that requires the prerequisite — derived from prereq.course_id | prereq_id: identifier for the course that is the prerequisite — derived from prereq.prereq_id
params.metric: No computed metrics in this view; it is a pure selection of base columns. (There are no aggregates or expressions; both output columns map directly to base table columns.)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a course dimension/view (e.g., a view that is one-row-per-course such as a course catalog view) on course_id or prereq_id — safe because that dimension is 1:1 per course and will not duplicate rows in this edge view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course_prereq_edges (REC) or other edge/graph views that are also one-row-per-edge on (course_id, prereq_id) — safe because they share the same grain (edge) and will not multiply measures. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as section_with_course_instructor_room_time, takes_with_student_course_section, or instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester without first aggregating those tables to the same grain (course_id or prereq_id) — otherwise rows from those many-side tables will multiply these edge rows and produce duplicated counts/measures. | When you need counts (e.g., number of prerequisites per course), perform an explicit aggregation grouped by course_id after joining or directly aggregate this view (e.g., SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS num_prereqs FROM course_prereq_links GROUP BY course_id) — do not rely on implicit multiplicative joins to compute metrics. | When joining to aggregated metrics from sibling AGG views (e.g., course_offering_counts_by_term, course_popularity_by_enrollment), join on course_id or prereq_id as appropriate — safe because those AGG views are pre-aggregated to a course-level grain; ensure you join to the correct course key (course_id vs prereq_id) to keep semantics clear. | If you need attributes from both sides of the edge, join course_prereq_links twice to the course dimension/view (aliasing for course and prereq) — safe because each join is 1:1 per course and will not duplicate edge rows.

views.description: Lists direct prerequisite links between courses (one row per course -> prerequisite course pair).

views.name: course_with_prereq_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.prereq_id) AS distinct_prereq_count
FROM
  course c
LEFT JOIN
  prereq p
ON
  c.course_id = p.course_id
GROUP BY
  c.course_id

params.description: For each course, how many distinct prerequisite records (prereq_id) are associated with that course.
params.when_to_use: Get the count of distinct prerequisites for a given course_id or a list of courses. | Rank or filter courses by how many distinct prerequisites they have. | Join with course-level information (title, department) without risking duplication of the prerequisite count. | Compose into higher-level aggregations (e.g., average prereq count per department) by treating this view as one-row-per-course pre-aggregated data.
params.output_schema: course_id: unique identifier for a course; derived from base table column course.course_id | distinct_prereq_count: number of distinct prereq_id values linked to the course; derived from COUNT(DISTINCT prereq.prereq_id)
params.metric: distinct_prereq_count = COUNT(DISTINCT prereq.prereq_id) grouped by course.course_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course (base table) on course_id — safe because course_with_prereq_counts has exactly one row per course_id, so joining back to course (one row per course_id) does not duplicate the measure. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course_offering_counts_by_term (AGG) on course_id — safe to join when you need to combine course-level aggregates; both sides are one-row-per-course (or one-row-per-course-per-term for offering counts: if joining to per-term rows, be aware offering rows are per term and will multiply rows per course per term intentionally). If you want per-term counts combined with this view, aggregate or filter appropriately to avoid unintended multiplication. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester (RANK) only when you plan to join at the course_id level and accept that instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester may be one-to-many by (course_id, year, semester); to avoid duplicating distinct_prereq_count, first reduce instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester to one row per course_id (e.g., by selecting latest/representative row) before joining. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail tables/views (e.g., takes_with_student_course_section, section_with_course_instructor_room_time, student_enrollment_counts if it is per-student-per-course) without re-aggregation — joining a one-row-per-course pre-aggregated view to a table that has multiple rows per course will duplicate distinct_prereq_count across those multiple rows and thus inflate measures unless you re-aggregate after the join. | If you need to compose with course_prereq_edges (REC) which lists individual prerequisite edges, avoid joining it back to this aggregated view on course_id unless you intend to expand to per-edge granularity; to preserve the aggregate, either (a) join only to course (one-to-one) or (b) re-aggregate after joining (e.g., SUM DISTINCT_PREREQ_COUNT by course_id is unnecessary, but if joining to edges you should compute metrics at the desired grain). | When combining into higher-level aggregates (department, term, instructor), first ensure the other side is reduced to one row per course_id (by aggregating or selecting a single representative row) so that SUM(distinct_prereq_count) over courses equals the true total of distinct prereq counts per course without double-counting. | In short: safe to join to any dimension or view that is one-row-per-course_id. Avoid direct joins to any view/table that is many-rows-per-course_id unless you re-aggregate after the join to the intended grain.

views.description: For each course, how many distinct prerequisite records (prereq_id) are associated with that course.

views.name: course_basic_50
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.credits AS credits,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name
FROM course

params.description: Basic canonical catalog of courses (one row per course) with id, title, credits, and department name.
params.when_to_use: Look up course metadata by course_id or department | Join course metadata to enrollment/section aggregates to annotate counts or metrics with course title/credits | Filter or group by course attributes (dept_name, credits) when composing higher-level reports | Serve as the dimensional (master) course table when building course-level aggregations
params.output_schema: course_id: unique identifier for a course — derived directly from base column course.course_id | title: course title — derived directly from base column course.title | credits: numeric credit value for the course — derived directly from base column course.credits | dept_name: name of the department offering the course — derived directly from base column course.dept_name
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view; all outputs are direct base columns (identity projections).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/one-row-per-key views or tables on course_id — safe because course_basic_50 is one-row-per-course (grain = course_id) so its attributes will not be duplicated. Example safe joins: join course_basic_50 to course_offering_counts_by_term on course_id if that aggregated view returns one row per course per term; in that case the offering counts are pre-aggregated and joining will not duplicate course_basic_50 rows beyond the term granularity. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to section_with_course_instructor_room_time on course_id only if you intend to expand to section-level detail (this is a one-to-many relationship: one course -> many sections). Such a join WILL multiply course_basic_50 rows per section. If you need aggregated course-level measures after joining to sections, re-aggregate (GROUP BY course_id) to return to one row per course. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to takes_with_student_course_section, instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester, student_enrollment_counts, course_prereq_edges, or any other one-to-many view/table that returns multiple rows per course — doing so will duplicate course-level attributes/metrics. Instead, either (a) join to pre-aggregated (one-row-per-course) views such as course_popularity_by_enrollment or course_offering_counts_by_term (when those are produced at course granularity), or (b) aggregate the one-to-many side to course_id before joining. | When joining to department-level aggregates (for example instructor_salary_by_department) join on dept_name — safe only if instructor_salary_by_department is one-row-per-department. If that departmental view is aggregated to one row per dept_name then the join will not duplicate course rows; if that departmental view is one-to-many, re-aggregate it first. | When composing metrics that count or sum across related tables (sections, enrollments, prerequisites), compute those metrics on the many-side (e.g., section or takes) with an explicit GROUP BY course_id, then join the resulting one-row-per-course aggregation to course_basic_50 to avoid multiplication. | Summary rule: treat course_basic_50 as a stable course dimension (one row per course_id). It is safe to join to it from an already-aggregated fact at course_id granularity or to join it to other single-row-per-course tables. It is unsafe to join it directly to one-to-many facts if you expect to preserve course-level cardinality — you must re-aggregate the many side to course_id first.

views.description: Basic canonical catalog of courses (one row per course) with id, title, credits, and department name.

views.name: course_prereq_counts_51
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT prereq.prereq_id) AS prereq_count
FROM course
LEFT JOIN prereq ON course.course_id = prereq.course_id
GROUP BY course.course_id

params.description: Per-course count of distinct prerequisite records (one row per course_id).
params.when_to_use: Get how many distinct prerequisites exist for each course. | Filter or rank courses by number of prerequisites. | Compose with course dimension data (title, department) to report prerequisites per course. | Join into higher-level reports (e.g., by department or term) where course-level prereq counts are an input metric.
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier for the course — sourced from course.course_id in the base table referenced by this view. | prereq_count: integer count of distinct prerequisite records for that course — derived from COUNT(DISTINCT prereq.prereq_id) over prereq.prereq_id.
params.metric: prereq_count = COUNT(DISTINCT prereq.prereq_id)  -- count of unique prereq.prereq_id per course.course_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course (or any one-row-per-course dimension/view) on course_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-course_id so joining to another one-row-per-course dataset will not duplicate prereq_count. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sibling views that are also aggregated at course_id (for example a hypothetical course-level aggregate) on course_id — safe because both sides are one-row-per-course and will not multiply measures. | do NOT join directly to prereq (the base prereq table) or any other one-to-many table keyed by course_id (without re-aggregating) because prereq_count was computed by aggregating prereq rows already; joining back to prereq will multiply rows and duplicate/over-count prereq_count. | do NOT join to one-to-many derived views (for example, section lists, offerings by term, takes_with_student_course_section, course_prereq_edges if it is one-to-many per course) on course_id without first aggregating those views to course_id level — otherwise the per-course prereq_count will be repeated for each child row and any further aggregation will overcount unless you explicitly re-aggregate prereq_count (e.g., by taking MAX or SUM(DISTINCT) as appropriate). | If combining this view into aggregates at a higher grain (e.g., department or term), first ensure the join path is to a course → department mapping (one-to-one per course) or aggregate the other side to course_id before joining, then sum prereq_count across courses to produce department-level prerequisite totals.

views.description: Per-course count of distinct prerequisite records (one row per course_id).

views.name: department_budget_summary_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  department.dept_name AS dept_name,
  department.building AS building,
  SUM(department.budget) AS budget_total,
  COUNT(department.budget) AS budget_count,
  AVG(department.budget) AS budget_avg
FROM department
GROUP BY department.dept_name, department.building

params.description: Aggregated department budget metrics summarized at the (dept_name, building) level.
params.when_to_use: When you need total, count, or average of department.budget grouped by department name and building. | As a pre-aggregated foundation when composing higher-level reports by building or by department (e.g., building budget rollups, department budget comparisons across buildings). | When joining department-level budget summaries to dimension tables that are one-row-per-building or one-row-per-department, without risking double-counting.
params.output_schema: dept_name: department.dept_name — the department name used as a grouping key (source: department.dept_name). | building: department.building — the building name/location used as a grouping key (source: department.building). | budget_total: SUM(department.budget) — total budget summed across all department rows for the given (dept_name, building) group (source: aggregate SUM on department.budget). | budget_count: COUNT(department.budget) — count of non-null department.budget values in the group (source: aggregate COUNT on department.budget). | budget_avg: AVG(department.budget) — average budget value for the group (source: aggregate AVG on department.budget).
params.metric: budget_total = SUM(department.budget) | budget_count = COUNT(department.budget) | budget_avg = AVG(department.budget)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a building-level dimension (e.g., classroom_location_normalized or classroom_rows if they are one-row-per-building) on department.building — safe because this view is one-row-per-(dept_name, building) and joining on building to a one-row-per-building dimension will not duplicate budget measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to an instructor_salary_by_department (AGG) view on department.dept_name and department.building only if that sibling view is also aggregated at the same keys — safe because measures are aligned at the same grain (one-row-per-(dept_name, building)). | do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables or views such as takes_with_student_course_section, section_with_course_instructor_room_time, student_enrollment_counts, or course_offering_counts_by_term without re-aggregation — those are one-to-many relative to this view's grain and will multiply budget_total/budget_count/budget_avg unless you first aggregate the child side back to (dept_name, building) or perform appropriate grouping after the join. | If you must combine with one-to-many siblings, aggregate the child relation to the same (dept_name, building) keys (e.g., SUM(enrollment) GROUP BY dept_name, building) before joining, or join first and then re-aggregate budget measures with GROUP BY dept_name, building to avoid double-counting. | Avoid joining on non-unique keys inside department (e.g., joining only on dept_name if dept_name appears in multiple buildings) unless you intend to widen or re-aggregate; joining on dept_name alone can duplicate building-level measures if multiple building rows exist for that department. | This view's measures are additive at the (dept_name, building) grain; safe aggregations on top include SUM(budget_total) or weighted recalculation using budget_count as weights. Do not assume budget_avg is a rollup-safe average without using budget_total and budget_count to recompute across groups (i.e., global_avg = SUM(budget_total)/SUM(budget_count)).

views.description: Aggregated department budget metrics summarized at the (dept_name, building) level.

views.name: courses_without_prereqs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id,
  c.title,
  c.dept_name,
  c.credits
FROM course AS c
LEFT JOIN prereq AS p
  ON c.course_id = p.course_id
WHERE p.course_id IS NULL

params.description: List of courses that have no prerequisites (one row per course).
params.when_to_use: Get all courses that do not require any prerequisite. | Filter or join when you need a canonical set of courses guaranteed to have zero prereq relationships. | Compose higher-level queries that count, report, or join other single-row-per-course attributes for courses without prerequisites.
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier of the course (derived from table course.course_id) | title: human-readable course title (derived from table course.title) | dept_name: department offering the course (derived from table course.dept_name) | credits: credit value for the course (derived from table course.credits)
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are produced by this view; all output columns are direct projections from course (course_id, title, dept_name, credits). The view implements a filter: selects course rows for which NOT EXISTS a corresponding prereq row (WHERE prereq.course_id IS NULL after LEFT JOIN).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like, one-row-per-course objects on course_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-course. Examples: join to course_prereq_edges only for enrichment with prereq edge attributes if you first aggregate or filter appropriately; however joining course_prereq_edges directly would create multiple rows per course (one per edge) and thereby multiply rows. | Safe to join to: section_with_course_instructor_room_time on course_id if you intend to expand into sections (this will create one row per section — expected expansion). Because this view is one-row-per-course, it will not itself duplicate measures, but the result will have one row per (course,section). | Safe to join to: course_offering_counts_by_term (aggregate per course) on course_id — safe because both sides are at course granularity and will not duplicate measures. | Safe to join to: course_popularity_by_enrollment (aggregate per course) on course_id — safe because both sides are aggregated to course level. | Unsafe to join without re-aggregation (will duplicate course rows/measures): any raw one-to-many tables keyed by course_id such as prereq, section (if you expect to preserve one-row-per-course), takes_with_student_course_section, instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester, student_latest_advisor (if multiple advisors per student-course context exist), classroom_rows if multiple matching locations exist. If you join to one-to-many sources, re-aggregate (GROUP BY course_id) or deduplicate the many-side first. | If composing counts or sums over this view, perform aggregation after any join that expands rows (e.g., count distinct course.course_id to preserve course-level cardinality, or aggregate the joined table by course_id before joining). | Do NOT assume this view encodes explicit absence of prereq rows beyond the prereq.course_id check used here; rely on course.course_id as the grain and treat any subsequent join that introduces multiple matching rows as a row expansion requiring re-aggregation if you wish to keep course-level measures.

views.description: List of courses that have no prerequisites (one row per course).

views.name: sections_with_classroom

  section_with_course_instructor_room_time.dept_name AS dept_name,

params.description: Lists distinct classroom assignments (department, building, room) for specific course sections (course_id, sec_id) offered in a given semester and year.
params.when_to_use: Find which department classrooms were used by specific course sections in a term or across terms | Filter or join course sections to the physical room (building/room_number) where they met | Compose schedules or room-utilization reports that start from section-level classroom assignments | Restrict downstream queries to the set of (dept_name, building, room_number) that hosted particular course sections
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name — derived from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.dept_name | building: building identifier/name where the section met — derived from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.building | room_number: room number where the section met — derived from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.room_number | course_id: course identifier for the section — derived from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.course_id | sec_id: section identifier within the course — derived from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.sec_id | semester: academic semester when the section was offered — derived from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.semester | year: academic year when the section was offered — derived from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.year
params.metric: No aggregated measures are produced by this view; all outputs are passthrough/non-aggregated columns. (There are no derived aggregate metrics like counts or sums.)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like, one-row-per-key views/tables such as classroom_rows or classroom_location_normalized on (building, room_number) — safe because department_classrooms_for_courses is one-row-per-(dept_name, building, room_number, course_id, sec_id, semester, year) and joining to a single-row classroom dimension will not multiply rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course_prereq_edges (if used as a lookup) only when matching on course_id and treating that view as a lookup of course relationships; ensure the prereq view is one-row-per-edge, and be aware this will produce one output row per prereq edge (i.e., intentional expansion). | DO NOT blindly join to one-to-many analytic/aggregate views (for example: student_enrollment_counts, course_offering_counts_by_term, course_popularity_by_enrollment, instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester) without re-aggregation, because those views contain aggregated counts or multiple rows per section/course/term and will multiply rows or double-count measures when joined directly. If you need counts (enrollment, offerings) per section/room, first aggregate those metrics at the same grain as this view (course_id, sec_id, semester, year, building, room_number, dept_name) and then join. | When joining to instructor-related views (e.g., instructor_salary_by_department or instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester or section_with_course_instructor_room_time's instructor columns), join on keys (dept_name or course_id + sec_id + semester + year) only if the target side is known to be one-row-per-key; otherwise pre-aggregate or deduplicate instructor rows to the section grain to avoid duplicating the section-level rows. | If you need to compute room-level aggregates (e.g., number of sections per room in a term), aggregate this view grouping by (dept_name, building, room_number, semester, year) to produce counts; do not join this view to another table and then count without grouping because that may double-count when the join creates multiplicity. | In short: safe to join to single-row dimension/lookups on (building, room_number) or (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) after confirming those sides are one-row-per-key. Avoid direct joins to one-to-many analytic views or raw enrollment lists unless you re-aggregate to this view's grain first.

views.description: Lists distinct classroom assignments (department, building, room) for specific course sections (course_id, sec_id) offered in a given semester and year.

views.name: department_course_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  COUNT(c.course_id) AS dept_course_count
FROM
  department d
LEFT JOIN

ON

GROUP BY

params.description: Counts of courses offered by each department (one row per department with the number of courses in that department).
params.when_to_use: Ask: How many distinct courses exist in each department? | Compose: Use as a departmental-level metric (dept_course_count) when building higher-level reports by department. | Compose: Join to department-level dimensions (e.g., department details) without re-aggregation. | Guard: Do not directly join to student/section-level tables and assume dept_course_count remains correct unless you re-aggregate.
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (derived from department.dept_name, the grouping key in the view) | dept_course_count: count of courses assigned to the department (derived from COUNT(course.course_id) in the view)
params.metric: dept_course_count = COUNT(course.course_id) aggregated at the grain of department.dept_name
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department (base table) on department.dept_name = department_course_counts.dept_name — safe because department_course_counts has exactly one row per department (one-row-per-dept_name) so the measure dept_course_count will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department-level or one-row-per-department views (e.g., instructor_salary_by_department) on dept_name — safe because both sides are aggregated at the department grain. | UNSAFE: do NOT join department_course_counts directly to one-to-many tables or views keyed by dept_name without re-aggregation (examples: course, section_with_course_instructor_room_time, takes_with_student_course_section, student_enrollment_counts if expanded by student, instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester, course_prereq_edges) because those joins will duplicate dept_course_count across multiple matching rows and inflate totals. | SAFE composition pattern when combining with lower-grain data: if you need department counts together with detailed rows (e.g., sections or enrollments), either (a) join this view to a department-dimension and keep dept_course_count as an additive attribute at department-level only, or (b) re-aggregate after joining (for example, SUM(dept_course_count) is only meaningful if you first deduplicate departments or group again at department granularity). | If you need to compute per-course ratios or per-section metrics, join at course_id or section keys to source tables (course or section) and compute COUNTs or distinct counts at that lower grain rather than relying on dept_course_count to roll correctly after such joins.

views.description: Counts of courses offered by each department (one row per department with the number of courses in that department).

views.name: courses_rowlevel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course

params.description: Provides one-row-per-course metadata (id, title, department, credits) for questions about courses and for composing course-level analyses.
params.when_to_use: Get basic descriptive information about a course by course_id | List all courses with their department and credit value | Join course-level attributes onto aggregate analyses (e.g., enrollments, offerings) keyed at course_id | Compose into higher-level queries that need course metadata (title, dept_name, credits) per course
params.output_schema: course_id: unique identifier for the course, derived from course.course_id | title: human-readable course title, derived from course.title | dept_name: department offering the course, derived from course.dept_name | credits: number of credit hours for the course, derived from course.credits
params.metric: course_id = course.course_id | title = course.title | dept_name = course.dept_name | credits = course.credits
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to section_with_course_instructor_room_time on course_id — safe because courses are one-row-per-course and section_with_course_instructor_room_time is a many-sections-per-course view; when joining, do not expect course-level measures to be aggregated by the join unless you aggregate sections first (joining will replicate the course row per matching section). If you need course-level measures preserved, aggregate the section side (e.g., count sections per course) before or after joining. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to takes_with_student_course_section on course_id — not safe to join naïvely if you expect one-row-per-course output because takes_with_student_course_section is many-students-per-course; joining will duplicate course rows for each enrollment. To preserve course grain, pre-aggregate enrollments (e.g., enrollment_count by course_id) and then join that aggregated result to this view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course_prereq_edges on course_id = prereq_course_id or course_id = course_id — course_prereq_edges is a relationship edge list (potentially multiple edges per course). Do not join without aggregation if you need one-row-per-course; instead aggregate prereq counts or materialize as a separate relationship table. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor_salary_by_department on dept_name — safe for bringing department-level aggregates onto courses because instructor_salary_by_department is aggregated by department. Since department is many-courses-to-one-department, joining this aggregated dept-level view will not duplicate course rows or multiply course-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course_offering_counts_by_term on course_id — course_offering_counts_by_term is aggregated (offerings by term). If that view is aggregated per (course_id, term) it will produce multiple rows per course; to avoid duplicating course rows, aggregate offerings across terms to course-level first or include term in downstream grain. Joining an already aggregated-by-course result is safe. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to student_enrollment_counts on course_id — student_enrollment_counts is an aggregate; if it is per course, joining is safe (one row per course). If it is per (course, student) or per term, pre-aggregate to course-level before joining. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester only if you include the ranking keys (year, semester, instructor) in the downstream grain; otherwise this is many-rows-per-course and will duplicate course rows. Aggregate instructor/section data to course-level before joining if you need one row per course. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to student_latest_advisor on course_id — likely not directly related (student_latest_advisor is student-level); do not join without an explicit key mapping and aggregation since it will multiply rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to time_slot_readable or classroom_rows or classroom_location_normalized only after joining through section or instructor/room-level views that relate sections to courses; these are dimension-like but are reached via sections (one course -> many sections -> many times/rooms). To avoid duplication, aggregate or join through an already-aggregated section-level result. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course_popularity_by_enrollment on course_id — safe if that view is aggregated to course-level (one row per course). If it is per (course, term) aggregate appropriately first. | Do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many detail table/view (sections, enrollments, prereqs, timeslots per section) when you expect to preserve one-row-per-course semantics — such joins will multiply course rows. Either (a) aggregate the detail side to course-level before joining, or (b) include the detail dimension in the query grain (i.e., produce a row per section or enrollment) and accept the finer grain.

views.name: prereq_edges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prereq.course_id AS course_id,
  prereq.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM prereq

params.description: Lists directed prerequisite edges between courses (one row per prerequisite relationship).
params.when_to_use: Find which courses are prerequisites for a given course (direct prerequisites). | Build course dependency graphs (direct edges) for pathfinding or curriculum checks. | Join to course metadata to label nodes when composing higher-level analyses of prerequisites. | Compose into transitive/recursive queries or aggregate counts of prerequisites per course.
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier of the course that has a prerequisite (derived from prereq.course_id) | prereq_id: identifier of the course that is a prerequisite for course_id (derived from prereq.prereq_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a course-dimension or course metadata view/table (e.g., a course table or any view keyed one-row-per-course) on course_id or prereq_id — safe because prereq_edges is one-row-per-(course_id, prereq_id) and those course-dimension rows are one-row-per-course, so joining will not duplicate prerequisite rows. | You may join prereq_edges.course_id = <course_table>.course_id to enrich the dependent course, or prereq_edges.prereq_id = <course_table>.course_id to enrich the prerequisite course — safe when the course table/view is one-row-per-course. | Do NOT join prereq_edges directly to any one-to-many table/view keyed to course_id (for example: section_with_course_instructor_room_time, takes_with_student_course_section, instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester) without first aggregating that table to one-row-per-course (or otherwise accounting for multiplicity). Such joins would multiply prereq_edges rows and thus duplicate counts/measures derived from this view. | If you need counts or other aggregates of prerequisites after joining to one-to-many details (e.g., sections or student enrollments), either (a) aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per course before joining, or (b) perform the join and then re-aggregate, being aware that prereq_edges rows will be repeated for each matching one-to-many row. | When composing transitive/recursive graphs (e.g., building course_prereq_edges(REC)), treat this view as the base edge set (one row per direct edge); recursive expansion should operate on these edges directly — no additional deduplication is required unless other joins introduce multiplicity.

views.name: courses_without_prereq_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  c.title AS title,
  c.dept_name AS dept_name,
  c.credits AS credits
FROM course c
LEFT JOIN prereq p ON c.course_id = p.course_id
WHERE p.prereq_id IS NULL
views.description: Cohort of courses that have zero prerequisites (derived by subtracting course IDs that appear in prereq). This is a reusable cohort for queries that need courses with no prereqs.

views.name: teaches_spring_year_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  teaches.ID,
  teaches.course_id,
  teaches.sec_id,
  teaches.semester,
  teaches.year
FROM teaches

params.description: A one-row-per-teaching-assignment view that lists each teaches record with its course/section and term (semester/year).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the set of teaching assignments for filtering, linking, or reporting by course, section, semester, and year. | Serve as a base (driving) relation when composing queries that need one row per teaches.ID, such as joining instructor or course dimension data without changing teaching-assignment cardinality. | Build higher-level aggregations (e.g., counts of sections taught) by grouping this view by semester/year/course_id.
params.output_schema: ID: identifier of the teaching assignment — comes from teaches.ID | course_id: identifier of the course associated with the teaching assignment — comes from teaches.course_id | sec_id: section identifier for the teaching assignment — comes from teaches.sec_id | semester: academic semester label for the teaching assignment — comes from teaches.semester | year: academic year for the teaching assignment — comes from teaches.year
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like, one-row-per-key views/tables on matching keys without duplicating measures: |  - Join to course-related single-row views/tables (e.g., classroom_rows if it were keyed by course_id) on course_id — safe because teaches is one-row-per-ID and course dimension is one-row-per-course, so teaches rows are preserved and not multiplied. |  - Join to student_latest_advisor (JOIN) only when keyed by instructor ID or student ID if that view is one-row-per-key; verify the sibling view's grain before joining. | Do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views that will multiply teaches rows unless you re-aggregate afterwards: |  - Do NOT directly join to takes_with_student_course_section (JOIN) without aggregation, because that view represents many student enrollments per section and would duplicate teaches rows (one teaches row per enrollment) and thus multiply any counts derived from teaches. |  - Do NOT directly join to course_prereq_edges (REC) if course_prereq_edges is many-per-course (prereqs graph), because joining on course_id would duplicate teaches rows for courses with multiple prerequisites. |  - Do NOT directly join to student_enrollment_counts or course_offering_counts_by_term unless you join on matching grain (e.g., semester+year+course_id) and understand whether those sibling views are aggregated and one-row-per-key; if they are aggregated to one-row-per-(term+course) then joining on the same keys is safe. | Guidelines for safe composition and re-aggregation: |  - If you need to combine teaches with a many-side relation (e.g., enrollments), either (a) aggregate the many-side to the teaches grain (group by course_id, sec_id, semester, year or by teaches.ID) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate grouping back to teaches.ID (or course/section/term) to avoid duplicated measures. |  - When composing metrics such as counts or sums, compute them at a stable grain: use this view's grain (teaches.ID or the tuple course_id+sec_id+semester+year) as the grouping key to ensure cardinality correctness.

views.name: teaches_with_instructor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  teaches.ID AS "teaches.ID",
  teaches.course_id AS "teaches.course_id",
  teaches.sec_id AS "teaches.sec_id",
  teaches.semester AS "teaches.semester",
  teaches.year AS "teaches.year",
  instructor.name AS "instructor.name",
  instructor.dept_name AS "instructor.dept_name",
  instructor.salary AS "instructor.salary"
FROM teaches
LEFT JOIN instructor
  ON teaches.ID = instructor.ID

params.description: Provides the teaches rows augmented with the instructor's identifying info (name, department, salary) — i.e., which instructor (by ID) taught each course section offering.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve instructor attributes (name, dept_name, salary) alongside each teaches row (course section offering) for reporting or filtering. | Filter or group teaches rows by instructor attributes (e.g., list course sections taught by a given instructor name or department). | Compose higher-level aggregations that count or summarize teaches rows while referencing instructor properties (but ensure correct aggregation when joining further). | Join with other dimension-like views on instructor ID to enrich or filter teaches rows without duplicating measures (when done on one-to-one keys).
params.output_schema: teaches.ID: instructor identifier for this teaches row — sourced from teaches.ID | teaches.course_id: course identifier for the taught section — sourced from teaches.course_id | teaches.sec_id: section identifier for the taught section — sourced from teaches.sec_id | teaches.semester: semester label for the taught section — sourced from teaches.semester | teaches.year: year for the taught section — sourced from teaches.year | instructor.name: instructor's full name — sourced from instructor.name (via LEFT JOIN on teaches.ID = instructor.ID) | instructor.dept_name: instructor's department name — sourced from instructor.dept_name (via LEFT JOIN on teaches.ID = instructor.ID) | instructor.salary: instructor's salary — sourced from instructor.salary (via LEFT JOIN on teaches.ID = instructor.ID)
params.grounded_columns: teaches.ID | teaches.course_id | teaches.sec_id | teaches.semester | teaches.year | instructor.ID | instructor.name | instructor.dept_name | instructor.salary
params.metric: This view exposes no derived numeric aggregates; instructor.salary is a base column (instructor.salary) projected through the LEFT JOIN — treat it as a base attribute, not an aggregated metric.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension views keyed 1:1 on instructor ID — e.g., join to student_latest_advisor or instructor_salary_by_department (if those are aggregated per instructor ID) on teaches.ID = <dim>.ID is safe because this view has one row per teaches row; joining to a one-row-per-instructor relation will not duplicate teaches rows. | Safe: join to time_slot_readable or classroom_location_normalized on section/time keys (if they are one-row-per-section/time slot) because those are dimension-like enrichments and do not multiply measures. | Do NOT blindly join to one-to-many relations such as takes_with_student_course_section, course_prereq_edges, student_enrollment_counts, course_offering_counts_by_term, or other aggregate views that are 1-to-many with respect to a teaches row without first aggregating them to the same grain. Such joins would multiply teaches rows and thus duplicate any measures derived from teaches (counts/sums). Instead, if you need aggregated information from those, first aggregate them to the teaches grain (teaches.ID, course_id, sec_id, semester, year) or join on fully matching keys and then re-aggregate. | When composing aggregations on top of this view (for example, counting sections per instructor or summing salaries), perform the aggregation after joining or explicitly GROUP BY the teaches grain columns to avoid accidental duplication. Example safe pattern: SELECT teaches.ID, COUNT(*) FROM teaches_with_instructor GROUP BY teaches.ID (counts sections per instructor). | If joining to instructor_salary_by_department (aggregated by department), join on instructor.dept_name = instructor_salary_by_department.dept_name — that is safe only if instructor_salary_by_department is one-row-per-department and you intend the department-level metric to apply to each teaches row; be mindful that department aggregates represent department-level measures and should not be summed back without adjusting for duplication.

views.name: section_term_details
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.course_id,
  s.sec_id,
  s.semester,
  s.year,
  s.building,
  s.room_number,
  s.time_slot_id
FROM section_with_course_instructor_room_time AS s

params.description: Provides the room, building and time-slot for each course section in a specific semester and year (one row per course section per term).
params.when_to_use: Look up where and when a particular course section meets (given course_id, sec_id, semester, year). | Compose schedules by joining section location/time info to other section-level data (instructors, enrollments, classroom attributes). | Filter or group analyses at the course-section-term grain (e.g., join to enrollment counts or instructor assignments).
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier for the course; derived directly from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.course_id | sec_id: section identifier within a course; derived directly from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.sec_id | semester: academic semester label for the offering (e.g., 'Fall'); derived directly from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.semester | year: calendar or academic year for the offering; derived directly from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.year | building: building code/name where the section meets; derived directly from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.building | room_number: room identifier within the building for the section; derived directly from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.room_number | time_slot_id: normalized time-slot identifier for the meeting time; derived directly from section_with_course_instructor_room_time.time_slot_id
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are produced by this view; all outputs are atomic base columns copied from section_with_course_instructor_room_time. | Derived measures should be computed after joining (for example, to get enrollment_count join to student_enrollment_counts on the section keys and use that view's metric).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to student_latest_advisor on (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) — safe if student_latest_advisor is one-row-per-section (does not duplicate this view's rows). Verify sibling view's grain before joining. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to time_slot_readable on (time_slot_id) — safe because time_slot_readable is a normalized lookup (one-row-per-time_slot_id), so it will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom_location_normalized on (building, room_number) — safe because classroom_location_normalized is a normalized classroom lookup (one-row-per-(building,room_number)). | UNSAFE without re-aggregation: do NOT directly join to takes_with_student_course_section or student_enrollment_counts (aggregation views that may be one-row-per-student-per-section or aggregated counts) without ensuring you either aggregate those views to the section-term grain or join on keys and then re-aggregate. Joining a one-to-many students-per-section table to this one-row-per-section view will multiply rows and overcount any measures derived from the section view. | UNSAFE without care: do NOT join to course_prereq_edges or course_popularity_by_enrollment (graph/aggregate at course-level) without aligning grains — these are course-level structures and may require grouping or windowing to avoid duplicating section rows across multiple related course rows. | When composing metrics: if you need section-level measures (e.g., enrollment_count), prefer joining to an aggregation view that is explicitly at grain (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) such as student_enrollment_counts if that view is aggregated to the same grain. If sibling aggregation is at a coarser grain (course or term only), aggregate or filter it to the section grain before joining. | General rule: this view is strictly one-row-per (course_id, sec_id, semester, year). Only join other one-row-per-(course_id,sec_id,semester,year) lookups or one-row-per-key dimension tables (time_slot_readable, classroom lookup). For one-to-many children (students, prerequisites, instructor lists) either (a) aggregate the child to the section-term grain first, or (b) join and then re-aggregate with DISTINCT keys to avoid multiplying measures.
